title: ADR-heavy close - iteration deliverable discipline (ADR 0006), containerization architecture (ADR 0007), dispatcher missing-model behavior (ADR 0008); 0.2.16 retrospective; 0.2.17 plan; 0.3 iteration charter; drift sweep; cascade re-run + Mercor pack assembly explicitly descoped

scope_notes.rescope_disposition: W4 ran under a re-scoped brief that replaced the original plan §W4 cross-model cascade re-run + Mercor reference-pack assembly with an ADR-heavy close-out targeting three substantive design decisions (iteration deliverable discipline, containerization architecture, dispatcher missing-model behavior) plus the iteration retrospective, the 0.2.17 plan opening with the new ADR 0006 convention, and the 0.3 umbrella charter. The original plan's hard gate blocker (clean Pillar 7 cascade re-run + Mercor pack assembled with runbook) was deliberately deferred per the W4 launch brief: the cross-model cascade re-run becomes its own future iteration whose deliverable explicitly is 'Pillar 7 defensible verdict on cross-family Auditor diversity'; the Mercor pack assembly graduates to a future iteration when an external consumer forces it. The re-scoping is documented explicitly in retrospective §4 and as a deviation_from_brief below; it is not a silent shift.
scope_notes.midway_check_in_protocol: W4 brief mandated a halt-and-surface midway check-in after bucket 4 (ADR 0008 drafting) because the dispatcher-missing-model decision surfaces substantive sub-decisions (env var name, hybrid host URL default, override parameter semantics, tier manifest path, production-leak monitoring rule placement) that need Kyle's input before becoming final. The midway check-in posted: ADR 0006 + 0007 status as Accepted (drafted), ADR 0008 status as Proposed (pending confirmation), recommended A+D hybrid decision rationale, and five surfaced sub-decisions for Kyle's redirect-or-confirm. Kyle confirmed core A+D hybrid, accepted sub-decisions 1/2/3/5 as drafted, redirected sub-decision 4 (tier manifest path: /opt/aho/tier.json → host-mounted ~/.config/aho/tier.json read-only into container), and added a new requirement: aho.deployment.mode resource attribute (development|production) emitted on every signal so the production-leak monitoring rule has a real signal to fire on. Both amendments applied to ADR 0008 before W4 continued.
scope_notes.adr_0007_amendment: Mid-iteration tier-threshold amendment per Kyle's W4 confirmation: original ADR 0007 thresholds were base <8GB / partial 8-24GB / full ≥32GB, which placed NZXTcos (8 GB) at the partial boundary and forced a 'despite native bare-host running partial-tier' caveat. Amended to base <12GB / partial 12-32GB / full ≥32GB. NZXTcos lands cleanly in base; tsP3 (16 GB) lands cleanly in partial; full stays unambiguously cloud-tier. The §NZXTcos categorization section was rewritten - historical bare-host partial-tier workarounds are documented as out-of-scope-for-containerized-deployment (legacy install.fish path stays available; container does not support those workarounds).
scope_notes.adr_0008_amendments: Two amendments applied per Kyle's W4 confirmation. (1) Tier manifest path: changed from container-internal /opt/aho/tier.json to host-side ~/.config/aho/tier.json mounted into container as read-only volume. Rationale: host-side `cat ~/.config/aho/tier.json` works without `podman exec`; observability tooling that isn't container-aware can still consume the manifest. install.fish stays the sole writer; container is read-only consumer. (2) New aho.deployment.mode resource attribute (values: development | production) sourced from the manifest's deployment_mode field, set by install.fish based on context. The future production-leak alert rule becomes the conjunction `aho.dispatch.hybrid=true AND aho.deployment.mode=production` - without this attribute the rule has no way to distinguish dev hybrid use (expected) from prod hybrid use (the violation). The attribute itself ships in 0.2.17 W2; the alert rule is still a carry-forward.
scope_notes.no_code_changes_in_w4: W4 ships zero source code changes, zero tests added, zero git operations. Deliverables are entirely artifacts/ entries (3 ADRs + 3 iteration docs + 1 acceptance archive). This is in line with the W4 brief's hard rules. test_results below records this as N/A explicitly rather than synthesizing a test run.
scope_notes.adr_numbering_protocol_held: ADR numbers determined by disk enumeration of artifacts/adrs/ at execution time, not pre-fabricated in W4 brief. Pre-W4 enumeration: 0001-0005 (aho-internal). Allocated sequentially: 0006 (iteration deliverable discipline), 0007 (containerization), 0008 (dispatcher missing-model). Final post-W4 enumeration: 0001-0008. No fabricated numbers; no out-of-sequence allocations.
scope_notes.cross_project_contamination_vigilance: Three ADRs land in W4 covering iteration discipline, containerization, and dispatcher behavior. Each surfaces a high contamination risk because container/registry/cloud terminology is shared across many projects. Vigilance held: (a) 11 Pillars (aho), not 10 (kjtcom); (b) ADR numbering follows aho's sequential convention, not any other project's; (c) container/podman/docker terminology is generic and not project-specific; (d) tier-detection language uses aho's three-tier (base/partial/full) framing, not any other project's tier nomenclature. Verified by grepping each ADR for 'kjtcom', 'IAO', '10 Pillars', any other contamination markers - zero hits.
scope_notes.ship_honesty_per_adr_0006: Retrospective §1.2 retroactively constructs the graduation criterion 0.2.16 was supposed to ship against. Honest read: 0.2.16 graduates against the retroactive criterion (5 of 6 lines fully met; line 6 - W4 audit archive - pending this submission's audit). The original plan's W4 cross-model cascade + Mercor pack are explicitly NOT in the retroactive criterion because they were re-scoped out mid-iteration. The retrospective makes this explicit; this is the structural answer ADR 0006 was designed to enable.

acceptance_checks.check: Bucket 4 - ADR 0008 (dispatcher missing-model behavior) drafted, status Accepted, with two mid-iteration amendments
acceptance_checks.evidence: artifacts/adrs/0008-dispatcher-missing-model.md exists. Status: Accepted (post-Kyle-confirmation at midway check-in). Date: 2026-05-01. Decision: Production deployment (AHO_DISPATCH_HYBRID_MODE unset) hard-errors with new typed exception ModelNotAvailableError(DispatchError) on missing family. Development deployment (AHO_DISPATCH_HYBRID_MODE=1) routes missing-family dispatches to host's native Ollama via configured AHO_DISPATCH_HYBRID_HOST_URL, default http://host.containers.internal:11434. Override parameter dispatch(..., on_missing='error|hybrid|fallback|cloud') with fallback/cloud reserved as NotImplementedError for future ADRs. Amendment #1 (Kyle redirect): tier manifest moved from container-internal /opt/aho/tier.json to host-side ~/.config/aho/tier.json mounted read-only into container; rationale that host-side cat works without podman exec for debugging and observability. Amendment #2 (Kyle add): new aho.deployment.mode resource attribute (development|production) sourced from manifest deployment_mode field, set by install.fish based on context - gives future production-leak alert rule the conjunction `aho.dispatch.hybrid=true AND aho.deployment.mode=production` to fire on. Five sub-decisions surfaced at midway check-in for Kyle redirect: AHO_DISPATCH_HYBRID_MODE env name (accepted), host.containers.internal:11434 default (accepted), on_missing= parameter (accepted), tier manifest path (REDIRECTED), production-leak alert rule placement (accepted as carry-forward, not ADR-binding).

carry_forward_candidates.detail: src/aho/pipeline/orchestrator.py reads tier1-roster-validation-0.2.15.json at cascade init and asserts each assigned model's operational/partial/compromised classification is role-compatible. RoleIncompatibleError raised on incompatible assignment unless explicit override. Paired with the cross-model cascade re-run (CF1) because the gate's acceptance is exercised by the cascade.

carry_forward_candidates.title: ADR 0008 production-leak monitoring rule
carry_forward_candidates.detail: Conjunction `aho.dispatch.hybrid=true AND aho.deployment.mode=production` fires when a hybrid-mode-enabled container runs in production deployment. The aho.deployment.mode resource attribute ships in 0.2.17 W2 (per ADR 0008 amendment); the alert rule itself is a follow-on deliverable. Naturally pairs with the W3-CF2 engine-selection ADR work - once an alert engine is selected and wired up, this rule lands alongside the existing five.
